paragraphs.text: For I would have you know how greatly I strive for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;
paragraphs.original: Θέλω γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι ἡλίκον ἀγῶνα ἔχω ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ καὶ ὅσοι οὐχ ἑόρακαν τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ἐν σαρκί,
paragraphs.translit: Thelō gar hymas eidenai hēlikon agōna echō hyper hymōn kai tōn en Laodikeia kai hosoi ouch heorakan to prosōpon mou en sarki,

paragraphs.text: that their hearts may be comforted, they being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, that they may know the mystery of God, [even] Christ,
paragraphs.original: ἵνα παρακληθῶσιν αἱ καρδίαι αὐτῶν, συμβιβασθέντες ἐν ἀγάπῃ καὶ εἰς πᾶν πλοῦτος τῆς πληροφορίας τῆς συνέσεως, εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ μυστηρίου τοῦ θεοῦ, Χριστοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: hina paraklēthōsin hai kardiai autōn, symbibasthentes en agapē kai eis pan ploutos tēs plērophorias tēs syneseōs, eis epignōsin tou mystēriou tou theou, Christou,

paragraphs.text: in whom are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ᾧ εἰσιν πάντες οἱ θησαυροὶ τῆς σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως ἀπόκρυφοι.
paragraphs.translit: en hō eisin pantes hoi thēsauroi tēs sophias kai gnōseōs apokryphoi.

paragraphs.text: This I say, that no one may delude you with persuasiveness of speech.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο λέγω ἵνα μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς παραλογίζηται ἐν πιθανολογίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: touto legō hina mēdeis hymas paralogizētai en pithanologia.

paragraphs.text: For though I am absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit, joying and beholding your order, and the stedfastness of your faith in Christ.
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ καὶ τῇ σαρκὶ ἄπειμι, ἀλλὰ τῷ πνεύματι σὺν ὑμῖν εἰμι, χαίρων καὶ βλέπων ὑμῶν τὴν τάξιν καὶ τὸ στερέωμα τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν πίστεως ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ei gar kai tē sarki apeimi, alla tō pneumati syn hymin eimi, chairōn kai blepōn hymōn tēn taxin kai to stereōma tēs eis Christon pisteōs hymōn.

paragraphs.text: As therefore ye received Christ Jesus the Lord, [so] walk in him,
paragraphs.original: Ὡς οὖν παρελάβετε τὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον, ἐν αὐτῷ περιπατεῖτε,
paragraphs.translit: Hōs oun parelabete ton Christon Iēsoun ton kyrion, en autō peripateite,

paragraphs.text: rooted and builded up in him, and established in your faith, even as ye were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.
paragraphs.original: ἐρριζωμένοι καὶ ἐποικοδομούμενοι ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ βεβαιούμενοι τῇ πίστει καθὼς ἐδιδάχθητε, περισσεύοντες ἐν εὐχαριστίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: errizōmenoi kai epoikodomoumenoi en autō kai bebaioumenoi tē pistei kathōs edidachthēte, perisseuontes en eucharistia.

paragraphs.text: Take heed lest there shall be any one that maketh spoil of you through his philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ:
paragraphs.original: Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς ἔσται ὁ συλαγωγῶν διὰ τῆς φιλοσοφίας καὶ κενῆς ἀπάτης κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, κατὰ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου καὶ οὐ κατὰ Χριστόν·
paragraphs.translit: Blepete mē tis hymas estai ho sylagōgōn dia tēs philosophias kai kenēs apatēs kata tēn paradosin tōn anthrōpōn, kata ta stoicheia tou kosmou kai ou kata Christon·

paragraphs.text: for in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily,
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ κατοικεῖ πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα τῆς θεότητος σωματικῶς,
paragraphs.translit: hoti en autō katoikei pan to plērōma tēs theotētos sōmatikōs,

paragraphs.text: and in him ye are made full, who is the head of all principality and power:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐστὲ ἐν αὐτῷ πεπληρωμένοι, ὅς ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλὴ πάσης ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐξουσίας,
paragraphs.translit: kai este en autō peplērōmenoi, hos estin hē kephalē pasēs archēs kai exousias,

paragraphs.text: in whom ye were also circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, in the putting off of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ;
paragraphs.original: ἐν ᾧ καὶ περιετμήθητε περιτομῇ ἀχειροποιήτῳ ἐν τῇ ἀπεκδύσει τοῦ σώματος τῆς σαρκός, ἐν τῇ περιτομῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: en hō kai perietmēthēte peritomē acheiropoiētō en tē apekdysei tou sōmatos tēs sarkos, en tē peritomē tou Christou,

paragraphs.text: having been buried with him in baptism, wherein ye were also raised with him through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead.
paragraphs.original: συνταφέντες αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ βαπτισμῷ, ἐν ᾧ καὶ συνηγέρθητε διὰ τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐνεργείας τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·
paragraphs.translit: syntaphentes autō en tō baptismō, en hō kai synēgerthēte dia tēs pisteōs tēs energeias tou theou tou egeirantos auton ek nekrōn·

paragraphs.text: And you, being dead through your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, you, [I say], did he make alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὑμᾶς νεκροὺς ὄντας ἐν τοῖς παραπτώμασιν καὶ τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν, συνεζωοποίησεν ὑμᾶς σὺν αὐτῷ· χαρισάμενος ἡμῖν πάντα τὰ παραπτώματα,
paragraphs.translit: kai hymas nekrous ontas en tois paraptōmasin kai tē akrobystia tēs sarkos hymōn, synezōopoiēsen hymas syn autō· charisamenos hēmin panta ta paraptōmata,

paragraphs.text: having blotted out the bond written in ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us: and he hath taken it out that way, nailing it to the cross;
paragraphs.original: ἐξαλείψας τὸ καθʼ ἡμῶν χειρόγραφον τοῖς δόγμασιν ὃ ἦν ὑπεναντίον ἡμῖν, καὶ αὐτὸ ἦρκεν ἐκ τοῦ μέσου προσηλώσας αὐτὸ τῷ σταυρῷ·
paragraphs.translit: exaleipsas to kathʼ hēmōn cheirographon tois dogmasin ho ēn hypenantion hēmin, kai auto ērken ek tou mesou prosēlōsas auto tō staurō·

paragraphs.text: having despoiled the principalities and the powers, he made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in it.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκδυσάμενος τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας ἐδειγμάτισεν ἐν παρρησίᾳ, θριαμβεύσας αὐτοὺς ἐν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: apekdysamenos tas archas kai tas exousias edeigmatisen en parrēsia, thriambeusas autous en autō.

paragraphs.text: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of a feast day or a new moon or a sabbath day:
paragraphs.original: Μὴ οὖν τις ὑμᾶς κρινέτω ἐν βρώσει ἢ ἐν πόσει ἢ ἐν μέρει ἑορτῆς ἢ νουμηνίας ἢ σαββάτων,
paragraphs.translit: Mē oun tis hymas krinetō en brōsei ē en posei ē en merei heortēs ē noumēnias ē sabbatōn,

paragraphs.text: which are a shadow of the things to come; but the body is Christ`s.
paragraphs.original: ἅ ἐστιν σκιὰ τῶν μελλόντων, τὸ δὲ σῶμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ha estin skia tōn mellontōn, to de sōma tou Christou.

paragraphs.text: Let no man rob you of your prize by a voluntary humility and worshipping of the angels, dwelling in the things which he hath seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,
paragraphs.original: μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς καταβραβευέτω θέλων ἐν ταπεινοφροσύνῃ καὶ θρησκείᾳ τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἃ ἑόρακεν ἐμβατεύων, εἰκῇ φυσιούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ νοὸς τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: mēdeis hymas katabrabeuetō thelōn en tapeinophrosynē kai thrēskeia tōn angelōn, ha heoraken embateuōn, eikē physioumenos hypo tou noos tēs sarkos autou,

paragraphs.text: and not holding fast the Head, from whom all the body, being supplied and knit together through the joints and bands, increasing with the increase of God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐ κρατῶν τὴν κεφαλήν, ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα διὰ τῶν ἁφῶν καὶ συνδέσμων ἐπιχορηγούμενον καὶ συμβιβαζόμενον αὔξει τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ou kratōn tēn kephalēn, ex hou pan to sōma dia tōn haphōn kai syndesmōn epichorēgoumenon kai symbibazomenon auxei tēn auxēsin tou theou.

paragraphs.text: If ye died with Christ from the rudiments of the world, why, as though living in the world, do ye subject yourselves to ordinances,
paragraphs.original: Εἰ ἀπεθάνετε σὺν Χριστῷ ἀπὸ τῶν στοιχείων τοῦ κόσμου, τί ὡς ζῶντες ἐν κόσμῳ δογματίζεσθε·
paragraphs.translit: Ei apethanete syn Christō apo tōn stoicheiōn tou kosmou, ti hōs zōntes en kosmō dogmatizesthe·

paragraphs.text: Handle not, nor taste, nor touch
paragraphs.original: Μὴ ἅψῃ μηδὲ γεύσῃ μηδὲ θίγῃς,
paragraphs.translit: Mē hapsē mēde geusē mēde thigēs,

paragraphs.text: (all which things are to perish with the using), after the precepts and doctrines of men?
paragraphs.original: ἅ ἐστιν πάντα εἰς φθορὰν τῇ ἀποχρήσει, κατὰ τὰ ἐντάλματα καὶ διδασκαλίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων;
paragraphs.translit: ha estin panta eis phthoran tē apochrēsei, kata ta entalmata kai didaskalias tōn anthrōpōn;

paragraphs.text: Which things have indeed a show of wisdom in will-worship, and humility, and severity to the body; [but are] not of any value against the indulgence of the flesh.
paragraphs.original: ἅτινά ἐστιν λόγον μὲν ἔχοντα σοφίας ἐν ἐθελοθρησκίᾳ καὶ ταπεινοφροσύνῃ καὶ ἀφειδίᾳ σώματος, οὐκ ἐν τιμῇ τινι πρὸς πλησμονὴν τῆς σαρκός.
paragraphs.translit: hatina estin logon men echonta sophias en ethelothrēskia kai tapeinophrosynē kai apheidia sōmatos, ouk en timē tini pros plēsmonēn tēs sarkos.
